I am 70, so I will keep my plan simple, familiar, and low-risk. In Quzhou County, the safest way for me is still the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation on most of my land, because I know this system well, the machinery and field work timing are clear, and it fits the local climate and irrigation conditions. I do not want a crop that needs too much fine management or too much market guessing. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and reliable, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is better. I will control fertilizer instead of using too much, because at my age I care about stable output, lower cost, and less trouble in the field. I will plough before wheat to manage straw and make a good seedbed, and use rotary tillage before maize so I can turn around quickly after wheat harvest. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in this area usually needs more water support, especially for overwintering and spring growth. I will spray only as much as needed to control the common weeds, aphids, and diseases, because too many pesticide applications cost money and add work. This year I will mainly grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, keep the work practical, and aim for stable grain yield rather than chasing the highest possible output.
